control: wrong fact (CED 9.2.A.1: electric potential is electric potential energy PER UNIT CHARGE)
title: Electric potential
body: Electric potential describes the total electric potential energy stored in a configuration of charges.
ced_evidence: 9.2.A.1: "Electric potential describes the electric potential energy per unit charge at a point in space."

control: explicitly excluded by the CED (9.2 BOUNDARY STATEMENT limits the charge distributions for which students use calculus to find electric potential; an arbitrary three-dimensional distribution is outside it)
title: Electric potential of an arbitrary three-dimensional charge distribution
body: Set up and evaluate a volume integral over an arbitrary non-symmetric three-dimensional charge distribution to find the electric potential at any point.

control: wrong owner topic (the electric potential energy of a system of two point charges is topic 9.1, EK 9.1.A.1-2; 9.3 covers changes due to a potential difference)
title: Electric potential energy of two point charges
body: The electric potential energy of a system of two point charges equals the work required for an external force to bring the charges to their current positions from infinitely far away.

control: reversed fact (CED 9.2.B.3.iii: an electric field vector points in the direction of DECREASING potential)
title: Field direction relative to potential
body: An electric field vector points in the direction of increasing electric potential.

control: hook expansion contradicts the CED (9.2.B.3.ii: isolines are PERPENDICULAR to electric field vectors; 9.2.B.3.iv: there is no component of the field along an isoline). The entry is correct, so only the hook should be rejected.
title: Isolines and electric field vectors
body: Isolines of electric potential are perpendicular to electric field vectors, and there is no component of an electric field along an isoline.

expands_to.means: the electric field is parallel to an isoline of equal potential

hooks.caution: State the geometry in CED terms when answering.

control: content from another unit (the behavior of charge on a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is Unit 10, EK 10.1.A.2; it is not in the Unit 9 pages)
title: Excess charge on a conductor
body: When a conductor is in electrostatic equilibrium, excess charge carriers reside entirely on its surface and the electric field inside is zero.
